answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether supplying willow saplings, quartz sensors, or terrace repairs. Each active identity needs its own bond, and locked funds cannot back another account. Creating 10,000 fake sellers therefore ties up $1 million for a month, imposing financing costs even if no fraud is detected. This makes identities cheap to name but costly to multiply.
